Using Ramsey theory, I know that an independence number of 3 is achievable on 10 vertices, and I'm considering taking the complete graph K₁₀ minus a perfect matching as a starting point, which would give an independence number of 2 and maintain high connectivity.

After exploring a few options, I realize the complete multipartite graph K₃,₃,₃,₁ works perfectly—it has exactly 10 vertices partitioned into four parts of sizes 3, 3, 3, and 1. The independence number equals the largest part size, so α(G) = 3, and the vertex connectivity is 10 minus the largest part, giving κ(G) = 7, which easily satisfies κ(G) ≥ 2.
